name: Kuşadası
title: Holidays in Kuşadası
intro: A lively Aegean resort near the ancient city of Ephesus, with sandy beaches, a busy cruise port and a pigeon-island castle. Here's what Kuşadası is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: A cruise ship in port at Kuşadası, with palm trees and turquoise water in front

facts.label: Time difference
facts.value: 2 hrs ahead of the UK (3 in winter)

facts.label: Entry
facts.value: No visa for up to 90 days

facts_note: İzmir airport is about 1 hour 15 minutes away. Your passport needs at least 150 days left on it when you arrive. Check entry rules and the latest travel advice on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: April, May, September and October are the best times, especially for visiting Ephesus before the heat. June to August are hot and sunny, ideal for the beach but tough for sightseeing in the middle of the day. Winter is cool and wet.

things.name: Ephesus
things.blurb: One of the best-preserved Roman cities anywhere, with the Library of Celsus and a vast theatre. Go early.

things.name: Pigeon Island
things.blurb: A little fortress on an island joined to the town by a causeway.

things.name: Ladies Beach
things.blurb: The handiest sandy beach, lined with cafés.

things.name: Dilek Peninsula
things.blurb: A national park of quiet coves and pine forest south of town.

things.name: Şirince
things.blurb: A hill village known for fruit wines and old stone houses.

things.name: House of the Virgin Mary
things.blurb: A small chapel on a wooded hill near Ephesus, a place of pilgrimage.

faqs.question: How far is Ephesus from Kuşadası?
faqs.answer: About 20 kilometres, a 25-minute drive or a short dolmuş ride to Selçuk.

faqs.question: Is Kuşadası good for a beach holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ladies Beach and Long Beach are sandy, and the national park beaches are quieter.

faqs.question: Which airport is closest to Kuşadası?
faqs.answer: İzmir, about 80 kilometres away. Bodrum is further, around 2 hours.

faqs.question: Can you go to Greece from Kuşadası?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ferries run to the island of Samos in about 1.5 hours in season.
